criteria.why: All formulas and numbers reproduce within 1%; F_peak of the system and F_egg of the egg are separated; sensitivity over k and n_crit is shown; minus 1.0 for merging the 60 mm free suspension stroke and the 96 mm cone crush into one stroke with 100% use of the cone height.
mass 458.0 g <= 500 g, sides 250x250x290 mm <= 300 mm, volume 0.018125 m3 <= 0.02 m3, cost $3.11 <= $5.00, build 28 min <= 30 min, materials only from the allowed list, egg not glued.

P1=0.943 for the nominal bottom-first landing and P3=0.730 for three drops with damage accumulation; minus 1.0 for a strong dependence on the 0.96 no-tumble probability for a blunt 250x250x290 mm box at 152 g side and 290 g top loads.

The physical role of all 12 materials and the dissipation mechanisms are explained and compared with three alternatives, but the buckling force of the paper cones and the rubber-band stiffness are not derived from material properties.

All masses, prices, part dimensions and closed 290 mm and 250 mm chains are given; minus 1.0 for blank-table inaccuracies: a single 250x250x3 mm cardboard sheet for the whole body, five 20 mm foam sheets for six sides with an 18 mm bottom layer, and a 4x4 cone matrix of 240 mm against a 204 mm gap between the side foam.

Concrete first-iteration calculations (two-stage block, k down to 1.15, peak down to 70.9 g; the 364 mm and 515 g proof against symmetric top reinforcement) and a full 20 m recomputation (v=19.81 m/s, Ek=89.86 J, d_min=200 mm, chains 334 mm and 299 mm).
